title: A speculative story set in Mumbai just won one of the world's biggest short-story prizes.

sources.text: Scroll.in - Three Indian writers make the Asian shortlist for the 2026 Commonwealth Short Story Prize
The Lagos Review - Commonwealth Short Story Prize 2026 announces regional winners

caption:
A speculative story set in Mumbai just won one of the world's biggest short-story prizes.

Her story 'Mehendi Nights,' a speculative tale set in Mumbai and published by Granta, was named the Asia region's winning entry when regional results were announced in May 2026.

Regional winners receive £2,500 each, with one of the five eventually named overall winner - Aruparayil's win put an Indian voice and an Indian setting at the center of one of the literary world's most internationally diverse competitions.

A speculative story set in Mumbai beating out entries from across the Commonwealth shows Indian fiction competing - and winning - on purely literary terms, not as a regional curiosity.
